chapter_title: Concerning the Man who is ugly in his Body, [but] beautiful [in his Soul].
chapter_note: The chapter opens with a hagiographic congregation scene and a moralizing address that culminates in a Gospel-derived saying (overlay). The oldest recoverable substrate concentrates in the impersonal, process-style teaching on pearl formation (¶9–13) and the cosmological return/rest of freed souls in the aeons (¶17). The explicit identification of the image with “the holy church” and “apostles” is an editorial application graft (¶15–16), followed by exhortation (¶18).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Scene-setting narrative with “the apostle” in a public gathering with teachers/elders/leaders; this is hagiographic container language, not impersonal cosmological exposition.

Institutional identity markers (“one of the elect”, “commandments”) and virtue-description (“holy righteousness”, “truthfulness”) anchor this in community discipline/edification rather than substrate cosmology.
Narrative development (homage, mocking crowd) in a story mode; no systematic cosmological mapping—functions as hagiographic exemplum.
Hagiographic portrayal of the revered figure (“the glorious one”) embracing the elect; physical staging and reverence cues indicate editorial narrative frame.
Speech-introduction formula in a congregational setting (“He says to them:”), continuing the narrative frame rather than substrate teaching.

Contains explicit NT/Gospel entry vector: “For the saviour says: … their angel sees the face of the Father daily.” Even where Manichaean terms appear (e.g., “Light Mind”), the paragraph’s climactic authority is a Gospel saying, marking this unit as later Christian overlay/homiletic use.
Crowd reaction and settling of the scene; narrative continuation (“all heard these words… while his disciples stand”) characteristic of compilation frame.
Formal disciple request (“Tell us, our master…”) is a standard dialogue prompt that frames the ensuing teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: “Pearls shall arise not in every place in the sea, nor be formed in the sea as a whole. Rather, in various places that are in this sea, pearls are formed in them [ ... ... ] that sea, in which the [pearls] shall be formed [ ... ] this [ ... ... ] what the sea shall [ ... ... ] its fire {blazes} above and comes [down ... ... ] and it makes foam like the drop of water that flows [ ... ] down in rainwater [ ... ] is the water [ ... ... d]own first [ ... ... ] foam and comes down [ ... ... ] the sweet waters [ ... ... ] the waters.
paragraphs.removed_material: +The enlightener says to them:+ (dialogue attribution / hagiographic frame marker).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The opening attribution is a later dialogue-frame seam, but the remaining unit shifts into impersonal, process-oriented exposition (“Pearls shall arise…”, causal steps), consistent with older teaching-style discourse rather than institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: “This drop of water shall [ ... ] down to the sweet waters and [ ... ] and they absorbed them and were combined with the [ ... ]. They did not [d]escend to the depths of the sea, but they [ ... ... ] it floated on the surface of the waters [ ... ... ] to it. The foam and the pearl-shell shall be formed [ ... ] this wholesome drop [ ... ... ] it, and it becomes a pe[arl ... ] that makes a drop of rainwater [ ... ] waters [ ... ] it not being whole. It breaks and separates out into many droplets, and it has time to become a drop of sweet water [ ... ] and comes up in the sea of [ ... ] rain and sweet water; and it is accomodated in the shell, which at first is foam. They shall be joined with each other at [this] time, and are shaped and become a great pea[r]l, a great and valued kind.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, stepwise “how it forms” exposition with no appeal to Gospel authority and no institutional identification; reads like a preserved teaching block.

paragraphs.core_text: “When, however, a drop of rainwater falls, and that drop breaks into many droplets and various {particles of water}, they shall be formed into and be confined in [n]umerous pearls, in the shell and the pearl-shell. One might form two pearls, another may form three, others may form five; some mould more than these, some fewer.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered/quantified variation within a natural-process teaching block; still impersonal and non-institutional.

paragraphs.core_text: “Now, when you might [find a] whole drop, and the shell receives it, it shall become a great and valued [pe]arl as its worth is perfected. [However], if these two droplets will have time (to adhere) to one another before any (water particle} escapes, and they mix with e[ach o]ther, and the shell [ ... ] before they break into [ ... ] within [ ... ] in a great kind [ ... ... ] the drop of rain, which [ ... ... ] another one, that [ ... ... ] the [w]aters form them in [ ... and] in a great, valued commodity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same technical, causal register; no shift into exhortation or church-identification, supporting an older instructional stratum.

paragraphs.core_text: “Behold, [I, I have] taught you how sea-pearls shall be formed. I have told you that as a pearl shall come into existence by means of rainwater that has [ti]me to become foam, the pearl-shell shall come into existence by means of the foam, and the foam itself comes into being by means of the transformation and the [ ... ] of the sea.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Closure of the technical teaching sequence (“I have taught you… I have told you…”), still without institutional mapping; functions as the end-cap of a self-contained exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: “Then immediately at the time when [ ... ... ] the pearl divers know it, they shall [ ... ] and they [ ... d]own to those places and they bring pearls up from the depths of the sea, and each pearl diver finds according to the fortune that is [ordai]ned for him. The pearl divers shall [gi]ve them to the traders, and the traders give them to the kings and the nobles.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Remains within the parable’s internal economy (divers → traders → kings/nobles) without yet identifying these as church offices; still ‘image-world’ description rather than editorial pointing-at.

Editorial seam into institution: “This is also what the holy church is like.” The correspondence crosses from image-world to contemporary ecclesial identity; per seam rule the whole paragraph is late application.

Continues the editorial application mapping using institutional terms (“apostles”) and interpretive identifications; even with cosmological nouns (“aeons of greatness”), the mapping’s target is church structure, indicating later graft.

paragraphs.core_text: “Fo[r a]ll the souls that ascend in the flesh of mankind and are freed shall be brought back to the great aeons of light. A place of rest comes about for them, at that place in the aeons of greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological-soteriological statement in system terms (souls, ascent, aeons, rest) without citation or institutional exhortation; reads as a compact substrate doctrinal kernel.
Direct second-person exhortation (“You too, my beloved ones, struggle…”) and promised reward language; application-voice concentration matches the chapter-end exhortative layer.
